name: chain-binding-closed-form
description: Exact two-constant closed form for the pure-chain binding, B(A) = E0*S_off(A0)*g^(A-A0)*(1-f^(A-1)), with f the corpus bond factor and g the free-trace growth per nucleon; plus the parameter-independent exclusion of the channel from extensivity.
scope: (b) for the extensivity exclusion (invariant: the closed form is geometric x (1 - geometric), never linear); (a) for the projections, which are NOT measured

assertions.name: the measured bond factor IS convention-D z, not merely near it
assertions.detail: atomic_tr_m_helium4_canonical.py defines f_pp = z_d, so this is the corpus's own constant appearing where it should — a consistency check on the construction, NOT a new identification.

assertions.name: closed form reproduces every measured point to <1e-25 relative
assertions.detail: worst relative error: pp 1.457e-30, nn 8.327e-31. A 2-parameter form matching 4 points at 1e-30 has no freedom left to fit with.

assertions.name: the two species sit on opposite sides of g = 1
assertions.detail: This is why my own 'both collapse' correction was wrong: it assumed the bounded-total hypothesis, which fails for pp. The Lean lemma was right and the premise I fed it was false.

assertions.name: the exclusion is stated with its Lean witnesses and is parameter-independent
assertions.detail: Both lemmas are sorry-free and generic in S, g, f — no substrate, no q, no anchor enters either statement.

assertions.name: the closed form yields two checkable predictions, labelled as projections
assertions.detail: pp marginal turns up at A=6; nn marginal changes sign at A=7. Neither is measured. Computing A=6 falsifies or confirms both.
